passages.heading: Rooted in Miami Gardens. Fighting for Our Future.
passages.text: Rooted in Miami Gardens and shaped by the people who raised him, taught him, and stood by him, Oliver Gilbert is running to give back to the community that made him who he is. Raised in Miami Gardens, educated in local public schools, and shaped by a lifetime of service to his community, he is running to build a stronger future for South Florida.

passages.heading: Rooted in Miami Gardens. Fighting for Our Future.
passages.text: His story is one of faith, perseverance, and service — from supporting himself as a college student and riding the bus to law school, to leading his growing hometown as Mayor and bringing safer neighborhoods, more parks, real economic growth, to fighting as a County Commissioner for better public transit, housing people can afford, and economic growth that benefits the entire region — his focus has always been on creating stronger neighborhoods, more resilient communities, and a better future for working families.

passages.heading: Rooted in Miami Gardens. Fighting for Our Future.
passages.text: At every step, his purpose has remained the same: to bring opportunity home and build a South Florida where every family has a fair shot.

passages.heading: Most people want the same things.
passages.text: They want to get to work without losing half their day. They want to see a doctor without dreading the bill. They want their kids to inherit an economy that rewards effort.

passages.heading: Their time back.
passages.text: A two-hour commute isn’t a transit problem. It’s a family problem, a cost problem, and a life problem.

passages.heading: Care they can afford.
passages.text: Nobody should wait until it’s too late to see a doctor because of the bill. Coverage isn’t a luxury. It’s a foundation.

passages.heading: A real shot.
passages.text: Small businesses and working families built South Florida. They deserve a federal government that builds with them — not around them.

passages.text: Congresswoman Wilson has fought for this community for decades, the last 15 years in Congress doing the hard work to move our community and country forward and she does not give her word lightly.

passages.heading: Donate Today
passages.text: She knows better than anyone what’s needed in Washington. I grew up right here in South Florida, in Miami Gardens. I know what families here are up against, because I have lived it. Rent that eats half a paycheck. Healthcare people cannot afford. A commute that swallows the day. I am running to change that. Not with promises, but with work.

passages.heading: Restore the American Dream.
passages.text: The HOME Act lowers monthly housing costs without weakening lending standards — helping responsible families own a home, build generational wealth, and gain long-term financial stability.

passages.heading: Restore the American Dream.
passages.text: And for the families locked out the longest — first-time and working-family buyers — it opens three more doors: expanded FHA lending, a homebuyer tax credit, and a cap on starter rates.

passages.heading: 01 / The Affordability Problem
passages.text: Millions of families can afford a home. They just can't afford this month's payment.

passages.heading: 01 / The Affordability Problem
passages.text: Home prices and mortgage rates have pushed monthly payments beyond what many hardworking families can carry — even when their income, credit, and employment are strong. The usual "fix" is to loosen lending standards, which is exactly what fueled past housing collapses. The HOME Act rejects that trade-off: it lowers the monthly payment without lowering the standards that keep lending sound.

passages.heading: Payments Outpace Paychecks
passages.text: Monthly costs have climbed faster than wages, putting a first home out of reach for qualified buyers.

passages.heading: A Closing Door
passages.text: Families who could once buy are now locked out, delaying the wealth-building that ownership provides.

passages.heading: The Wrong Fix
passages.text: Weakening underwriting to close the gap creates risk. Sound lending should never be the price of access.

passages.heading: 02 / How the HOME Act Works
passages.text: The HOME Act keeps traditional underwriting and simply restructures repayment. You qualify the way you would today. Your total cost is fixed at closing using a standard 30-year calculation. Then you choose how long to spread that fixed cost — which lowers what you owe each month.

passages.heading: Qualify the traditional way
passages.text: Income, credit, employment, debt-to-income ratios, and appraisals are all evaluated under today's 30-year underwriting standards.

passages.heading: Lock your total cost
passages.text: At closing, your interest rate and total repayment obligation are fixed using a traditional 30-year mortgage calculation.

passages.heading: Choose your schedule
passages.text: Spread that same fixed cost over a 40, 50, or 60-year payment schedule — whichever fits your budget.

passages.heading: Pay less each month
passages.text: A longer schedule means a smaller required monthly payment — freeing up room in the family budget.

passages.heading: Pay less each month
passages.text: Same total repayment. A longer schedule. A smaller monthly payment.

passages.heading: Pay less each month
passages.text: Your total repayment obligation does not increase because you selected a longer payment period. The longer schedule lowers the monthly amount, not the math behind it.

passages.heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
passages.text: Six principles hold the HOME Act together. Tap any item to expand.

passages.heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
passages.text: Borrowers qualify under existing 30-year underwriting standards. Income, credit, employment, debt-to-income ratios, and appraisals remain unchanged.

passages.heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
passages.text: The interest rate and total repayment obligation are fixed at closing. Borrowers choose a 40, 50, or 60-year payment schedule without increasing the total repayment obligation because of the longer schedule.

passages.heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
passages.text: Private lenders originate and service HOME mortgages. Treasury-backed housing bonds provide liquidity while participating lenders receive targeted federal tax credits.

passages.heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
passages.text: Qualified heirs may assume the mortgage without a forced refinance or interest-rate reset, preserving family stability.

passages.heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
passages.text: The HOME Act is paired with policies that increase housing production, streamline permitting, encourage workforce housing, support modular construction, and discourage institutional speculation.

passages.heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
passages.text: Families qualify at the traditional payment but benefit from a lower required payment, creating room to build emergency savings, retirement savings, education funds, home maintenance reserves, or small business capital.

passages.heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
passages.text: A lower required payment gives families room to breathe — to build emergency savings, retirement, education funds, home maintenance reserves, or the capital to start a small business.

passages.heading: 04 / The First-Time Buyer Package
passages.text: The HOME mortgage lowers the monthly payment. These three policies clear the other barriers — the down payment, the closing costs, and the rate itself.

passages.heading: 04 / The First-Time Buyer Package
passages.text: First-time buyers and working families face hurdles a lower payment alone can't fix: saving a down payment while paying rent, covering closing costs, and qualifying when rates spike. The HOME Act meets each one head-on. And every policy below follows the same rule as the HOME mortgage itself — more access, same sound lending standards.

passages.heading: Expanded FHA Lending
passages.text: FHA loans are how generations of American families bought a first home — low down payments, sound underwriting, and a public guarantee that makes lenders say yes. The HOME Act expands FHA lending for first-time buyers: loan limits that reflect what homes actually cost in communities like ours, lower mortgage-insurance premiums, and a simpler, faster approval process.

passages.heading: Expanded FHA Lending
passages.text: A first home with a down payment a working family can actually save.

passages.heading: Homebuyer Tax Credit
passages.text: A refundable federal tax credit for first-time and low-to-moderate-income homebuyers — real help with the down payment and closing costs that keep qualified families renting. The credit turns years of "almost enough" into keys in hand, and starts families building equity from day one.

passages.heading: Homebuyer Tax Credit
passages.text: Cash help at closing. Equity from day one.

passages.heading: Capped Starter Rates
passages.text: When interest rates spike, first-time buyers are the first ones priced out — families with strong income and credit watch the same house drift out of reach. The HOME Act caps the interest rate on qualifying first-time homebuyer mortgages, backed by the same public-private financing as the HOME mortgage: Treasury-backed bonds and lender tax credits cover the difference, so lenders stay whole and standards stay sound.

passages.heading: Capped Starter Rates
passages.text: The rate can't price a first family out of a first home.

passages.heading: BUILD Business Act
passages.text: America should not only be the best place in the world to work. It should be the best place in the world to start a business.

passages.heading: BUILD Business Act
passages.text: Small businesses are the backbone of the American economy. The BUILD Business Act modernizes the Small Business Administration by expanding access to capital, reducing barriers to entrepreneurship, and helping more Americans start, grow, and expand successful businesses.

passages.heading: 01 / The Challenge
passages.text: Too many entrepreneurs have the talent and determination to succeed but cannot access the capital needed to get started. The BUILD Business Act closes that gap by pairing affordable financing with mentorship, accountability, and streamlined government.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Eleven concrete actions to help Americans start, grow, and expand small businesses. Tap any item to expand.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Create the American Small Business Grant Program providing grants of $5,000 to $25,000 for equipment, inventory, software, licensing, insurance, lease deposits, and other startup costs.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Establish the SBA Growth Line offering low interest loans, generally from 0% to 2%, with deferred repayment.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Strengthen the SBA 7(a) program by increasing federal guarantees, reducing borrower fees, simplifying approvals, speeding processing, and expanding lending in underserved communities.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Strengthen the SBA 504 program by expanding funding, modernizing eligibility, speeding project approvals, and creating a new 504 Express Expansion track for established businesses creating jobs.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Create one digital portal for grants, loans, mentoring, technical assistance, and contracting opportunities.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Goal: Make government easier to navigate.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Partner with universities, chambers of commerce, Small Business Development Centers, experienced business mentors, minority business organizations, and local economic development agencies.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Publish annual reports measuring business creation, job creation, survival rates, loan performance, and taxpayer return on investment.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Simplify procurement and help more small businesses compete for government contracts.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Goal: Create reliable customers, not just affordable financing.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Reduce paperwork, simplify reporting requirements, coordinate permitting where possible, and expand digital services.

passages.heading: 02 / My Plan
passages.text: Goal: Let entrepreneurs spend more time growing businesses.

passages.text: Opening your first restaurant? Access startup grants and affordable financing.

passages.text: Buying your first commercial building? A strengthened SBA 504 program makes expansion easier.

passages.heading: Why This Matters
passages.text: The BUILD Business Act shifts federal policy from simply recruiting employers to creating more of them. When small businesses succeed, communities create jobs, families build wealth, neighborhoods become stronger, and America's economy grows from the ground up.

passages.heading: A Full Life. A Secure Future. A Promise That Lasts.
passages.text: Every person with a lifelong disability deserves healthcare, a safe home, meaningful relationships, and the support to live with dignity throughout every stage of life.

passages.heading: 01 / The Challenge
passages.text: For millions of families, the hardest question is not what happens today. It is what happens tomorrow.

passages.heading: 01 / The Challenge
passages.text: Parents of children with intellectual, developmental, and other lifelong disabilities often spend decades serving as caregivers, advocates, benefits experts, transportation coordinators, housing planners, and emergency responders. They hold together a system that was never designed to work as one system.

passages.heading: 01 / The Challenge
passages.text: When a child becomes an adult, families can face separate rules for Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, housing, employment services, transportation, and community programming. A parent may have to contact multiple agencies just to keep basic services in place.

passages.heading: 01 / The Challenge
passages.text: Then comes the question no family should have to face alone: What happens when the parent becomes sick, grows older, or dies?

passages.heading: 01 / The Challenge
passages.text: Too often, the answer is a crisis. Housing is disrupted. Caregivers disappear. Benefits lapse. Siblings are asked to take over without preparation. Adults who have lived in the community may face isolation or unnecessary institutional placement.

passages.heading: 01 / The Challenge
passages.text: That is not a system of care. It is a system of uncertainty.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: The CARE Act creates a comprehensive federal framework for lifelong care and community living. It brings existing programs together, fills the gaps between them, and ensures that every eligible person has one coordinated plan for life.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: No person should lose healthcare, housing, caregiving, or community because a parent can no longer provide care.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: The CARE Act is built around eight commitments . Tap any item to expand.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: Every eligible person will have one federally certified CARE Advocate beginning during the transition to adulthood and continuing throughout life. The CARE Advocate becomes the family's single point of contact and coordinates services across Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, housing, healthcare, transportation, employment, education, and community programs.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: What it means One person responsible for making sure the whole system works together.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: Eligible individuals will receive timely access to necessary home and community-based services, including personal assistance, nursing, therapies, behavioral healthcare, transportation, respite care, supported employment, day services, residential support, and emergency backup care.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: What it means Community care should be dependable, not something families wait years to receive.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: The CARE Act will expand accessible housing modeled after successful efforts such as Casa Familia, including supported apartments, small shared homes, mixed-income communities, independent living options, and higher-support residences. Housing funding and care funding will be coordinated instead of treated as unrelated programs.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: What it means The goal is not simply a bed. The goal is a home and a community.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: Community Belonging Grants will support programs that create real relationships and full community participation. That includes models similar to Friendship Circle, Best Buddies, Special Olympics, faith-based inclusion programs, arts, recreation, volunteer service, peer mentoring, and civic engagement.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: What it means A full life includes friends, places to go, people who know your name, and opportunities to contribute.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: Beginning in adolescence, each participant and family will create a Lifelong Support Plan covering housing, healthcare, communication needs, transportation, employment, daily support, emergency care, financial planning, future caregivers, and supported decision-making. The plan will follow the individual and be updated over time.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: What it means The transition after a parent's death should never begin with strangers trying to reconstruct a person's life.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: The CARE Act expands respite care, caregiver training, mental health support, sibling planning, legal and financial guidance, emergency caregiver networks, and transition assistance.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: What it means Parents should be allowed to be parents, not unpaid administrators of a broken system.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: The plan invests in direct support professionals through better reimbursement, competitive wages, training, career ladders, benefits, recruitment, retention, and emergency staffing.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: What it means A promise of care means little if there is no one available to provide it.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: The CARE Act will make assistive technology part of the basic support plan, including communication devices, smart-home systems, wearable health tools, remote monitoring chosen by the individual, adaptive robotics, mobility technology, accessible transportation, and digital care coordination.

passages.heading: 02 / The CARE Act
passages.text: What it means Technology should increase independence and safety without replacing human connection or personal choice.

passages.heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
passages.text: The CARE Advocate is the practical center of the plan. This person will not replace a parent, guardian, caregiver, doctor, or benefits agency. The advocate will make sure they are communicating and working from one coordinated plan.

passages.heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
passages.text: Helps the individual and family create and update the Lifelong Support Plan.

passages.heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
passages.text: Coordinates applications, renewals, and transitions involving Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, housing, employment, and transportation.

passages.heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
passages.text: Organizes annual meetings with the individual, family, caregivers, providers, and appropriate agencies.

passages.heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
passages.text: Maintains an emergency and successor-care plan.

passages.heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
passages.text: Tracks deadlines and prevents avoidable gaps in benefits or services.

passages.heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
passages.text: Helps resolve disputes and escalates urgent needs when agencies fail to respond.

passages.heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
passages.text: Monitors actual quality of life, not merely whether forms were completed.

passages.heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
passages.text: Remains accountable to the individual and respects supported decision-making, privacy, choice, and independence.

passages.heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
passages.text: Federal agencies will retain their legal authority over eligibility and benefits. The CARE Advocate will have statutory coordination authority, access to participating agencies with the individual's consent, and the ability to require timely responses and elevate unresolved cases.

passages.heading: 04 / One Lifelong Support Plan
passages.text: Every participant will have one secure, portable Lifelong Support Plan recognized across participating programs. The individual must be at the center of that plan, with family and trusted supporters involved according to the individual's preferences and legal rights.

passages.heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
passages.text: The CARE Act will establish continuous coverage and coordinated care for people with qualifying lifelong disabilities. Medicaid will remain the principal payer for long-term services and supports. Medicare will cover eligible medical services. Social Security will provide income support. The CARE Advocate will make those systems function as one plan instead of separate bureaucracies.

passages.heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
passages.text: Prevent unnecessary interruptions in Medicaid for people with permanent qualifying disabilities.

passages.heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
passages.text: Provide Medicaid wraparound coverage for services Medicare does not cover.

passages.heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
passages.text: Expand access to Medicaid Buy-In so people can work without losing essential care.

passages.heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
passages.text: Require coverage of emergency backup caregiving and transition support.

passages.heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
passages.text: Reduce repetitive paperwork and duplicative disability reviews where the condition is permanent.

passages.heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
passages.text: Protect continuity when an individual moves between communities or across state lines.

passages.heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
passages.text: The CARE Act will create a national Community Living Capital Fund to help nonprofit organizations, local governments, housing providers, and families build or preserve accessible community housing. The program will coordinate HUD housing resources, federal tax incentives, local land, nonprofit investment, and Medicaid-funded services.

passages.heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
passages.text: Federal support should be flexible enough to help create different options because adults with disabilities do not all need or want the same living arrangement.

passages.heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
passages.text: Small homes shared by a limited number of residents

passages.heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
passages.text: Supported apartments with staff available on site

passages.heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
passages.text: Mixed-income and mixed-ability developments

passages.heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
passages.text: Independent apartments with visiting support

passages.heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
passages.text: Residences designed for people with more significant medical or behavioral needs

passages.heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
passages.text: The standard must be dignity, safety, individual choice, and meaningful connection to the surrounding community. Community living cannot become institutional care with a nicer sign out front.

passages.heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
passages.text: One coordinated promise replaces a patchwork of disconnected programs. Here is the difference for families living it every day.

passages.heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
passages.text: One CARE Advocate coordinates the entire plan.

passages.heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
passages.text: Community services can depend on a waiting list.

passages.heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
passages.text: Necessary lifelong supports are guaranteed on a timely basis.

passages.heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
passages.text: Succession and emergency planning begin during adolescence.

passages.heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
passages.text: Housing, services, transportation, and community programming are coordinated.

passages.heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
passages.text: Parents worry about what happens when they die.

passages.heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
passages.text: A successor-care plan, stable housing, and a support team are already in place.

passages.heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
passages.text: Success is measured by safety, health, independence, relationships, purpose, and belonging.

passages.heading: 08 / How the Federal Government Will Work Together
passages.text: The CARE Act does not pretend that one existing agency can do everything. It gives each agency a clear responsibility and creates one coordinated system around the individual.

passages.heading: 09 / Protecting Choice and Preventing Abuse
passages.text: A stronger care system must also protect the rights of the people it serves. The CARE Act will include independent oversight, transparent reporting, background and training standards, accessible complaint procedures, protection against abuse and financial exploitation, and regular review of restrictive guardianships.

passages.heading: 09 / Protecting Choice and Preventing Abuse
passages.text: No housing provider, caregiver, guardian, or government agency should control a person's life simply because that person needs support. The individual's voice, preferences, safety, and right to live in the community must remain at the center of every decision.

passages.heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
passages.text: The federal government will be required to report whether participants are actually living better lives. Measures will include:

passages.heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
passages.text: Continuity of healthcare and support services

passages.heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
passages.text: Preventable hospitalizations and emergency placements

passages.heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
passages.text: Employment, education, volunteering, or meaningful daily activity

passages.heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
passages.text: Personal choice and supported decision-making

passages.heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
passages.text: Caregiver stability and workforce retention

passages.heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
passages.text: Avoidance of unnecessary institutionalization

passages.heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
passages.text: Perfect paperwork and an isolated life is not success.

passages.heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
passages.text: A parent's death will always be a profound personal loss. It should not also become a housing crisis, a healthcare crisis, and a caregiving crisis.

passages.heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
passages.text: The CARE Act will help adults build stable lives, homes, relationships, routines, and support networks while their parents are still alive. It will make sure the people who know and care for them are not replaced by a frantic search for services after a crisis.

passages.heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
passages.text: Independence does not mean facing life alone. It means having the support to live the fullest life possible.

passages.heading: 11 / Frequently Asked Questions
passages.text: No. A CARE Advocate coordinates programs and protects continuity. The advocate does not automatically control legal, medical, or financial decisions. Supported decision-making and the individual's own choices remain central.

passages.heading: 11 / Frequently Asked Questions

passages.heading: College ready. Trade ready. Life ready.
passages.text: Every student deserves a pathway to purpose. The BUILD Act prepares students for the economy of tomorrow by connecting education to real careers, expanding apprenticeships, supporting teachers, rewarding innovation, and building the workforce America needs to compete.

passages.heading: 01 / Why It Matters
passages.text: America cannot compete in tomorrow's economy with yesterday's education system. The BUILD Act recognizes that human capacity is infrastructure.

passages.heading: More Opportunity

passages.heading: On the Issues
passages.text: Gas is $5 a gallon, rent is half your paycheck, and every trip to the grocery store gets more expensive. For far too many neighbors, this has been the reality for far too long.

passages.heading: On the Issues
passages.text: Oliver Gilbert lived these challenges growing up in Miami Gardens, working his way through college and law school, and leading our city as Mayor and County Commissioner.

passages.heading: On the Issues
passages.text: What do President Trump and Washington Republicans do to help during these tough times? They spend your money on a war you didn’t ask for, didn’t vote for, and don’t need. They build a billion dollar ballroom for the Mar-a-Lago crowd. And they even use your own money to lie right to your face, spending millions on TV ads to deny the truth and divide our communities.

passages.heading: On the Issues
passages.text: South Florida families have had enough. It’s time to Put People First.

passages.heading: Healthcare For All
passages.text: We’re the richest country on earth, but we send billions of dollars to other countries so they can afford universal healthcare. How does that make sense? In Congress, Oliver will fight for a pathway to ensure that healthcare is a right for every American.

passages.heading: Eliminate Income Taxes for Working Families
passages.text: Families who are working hard to make ends meet shouldn’t have to carry the same tax burden as billionaires. The IRS should be spending more time auditing the ultra-wealthy than scrutinizing an Uber driver’s gas deduction. Oliver supports common sense tax policies indexed to what families in our communities actually earn, so that relief reaches the people who need it most and keeps money in working people’s hands.

passages.heading: Stop ICE Raids Now
passages.text: Our government has shamefully spent billions ripping families apart. They said ICE would only target criminals, but every day more and more hardworking people are being arrested and deported, often leaving young children behind to fend for themselves or leaving the only country they’ve ever known. It’s time to end funding for these shameful deportation policies and redirect that investment where it belongs: into our communities.

passages.heading: Universal Childcare & Pre-K
passages.text: Countries around the world have made universal childcare a reality. As a father, Oliver knows the challenges families are facing every day. In Washington, he will redirect spending toward our children and families, so that the resources no longer being wasted on mass deportations start building something that actually lasts.

passages.heading: Expand Rapid Transit
passages.text: In Congress, Oliver will fight to secure the federal funding needed to ensure the job gets done, and that our residents get the transit solutions they’ve been promised for decades.

passages.heading: Investing in Jobs & Job Training
passages.text: Oliver will fight in Washington to reinvest in job training, especially in high-paying technical fields that can’t easily be taken away by AI, and to strengthen support for entrepreneurs and small business owners.

passages.heading: From Miami Gardens
passages.text: I grew up here. I went to school here. I served here. And every step of that journey is the reason I’m running.

passages.heading: From Miami Gardens
passages.text: I was raised in Miami Gardens by two people who didn’t always see the world the same way. My mom was a Seventh-day Adventist teacher. My dad was a Baptist preacher. And in our house, I learned something early: people don’t have to agree on everything to love each other, to build a life together, to raise a family together.

passages.heading: From Miami Gardens
passages.text: They respected each other. They built something. That stayed with me.

passages.heading: Every Step in This Community
passages.text: Parkview Elementary. Parkway Middle. Miami Norland Senior High School. Every year of K through 12 happened right here. The teachers who taught me, the neighbors who watched me grow up, the friends who became family — they’re the reason I’m running, and they’re who I’m running for.

passages.heading: Tallahassee
passages.text: Florida A&M was my first real test. There were nights I lived out of my car. The work ethic and faith I brought from home are the only reasons I made it through. I learned that hardship isn’t something to perform — it’s something you live through, and what you do after defines you.

passages.heading: What Did You Learn Today?
passages.text: Law school meant a commute. I’d ride the 27 bus all the way down 27th Avenue to the Martin Luther King Metrorail station, then take the train to Coral Gables for class at the University of Miami School of Law. Some nights I’d get back late. And my dad would meet me at the MLK station. Every time. And he’d ask me one question.

passages.heading: “What did you learn today?”
passages.text: He wasn’t asking for himself. He wanted the knowledge to come back home. That question shaped everything I’ve done since.

passages.heading: Mayor of Miami Gardens
passages.text: I had the honor of serving as Mayor of my hometown for eight years. We worked on what mattered: safer neighborhoods, more parks, real economic growth, the kind of community policing that builds trust instead of breaking it. In 2020, Miami Gardens was named an All-America City — the first time in our history. I’m proud of that. But I’m more proud of what made it possible: a community that decided to invest in itself.

passages.heading: County Commission Chair
passages.text: On the County Commission, I’ve focused on a new goal: Make Miami-Dade County a truly world-class community. To get there, we have to overhaul our transportation system, which is why I’ve led bold initiatives to build up density along our transit corridors, creating partnerships that will fund rapid transit expansion and lead to more affordable housing in the neighborhoods that need it the most.

passages.heading: Why I’m Running for Congress
passages.text: What I’ve seen serving this community is simple. People want the same things. Good schools. Healthcare they can actually access. A commute that doesn’t take their life from them. A small business that can compete. A future their kids can build on.

passages.heading: Why I’m Running for Congress
passages.text: That’s what this campaign is about. Not running against anyone. Running toward something. Building a future that works for everyone, across South Florida.

passage.heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
passage.text: The CARE Act will establish continuous coverage and coordinated care for people with qualifying lifelong disabilities. Medicaid will remain the principal payer for long-term services and supports. Medicare will cover eligible medical services. Social Security will provide income support. The CARE Advocate will make those systems function as one plan instead of separate bureaucracies.

passage.heading: Restore the American Dream.
passage.text: The HOME Act lowers monthly housing costs without weakening lending standards — helping responsible families own a home, build generational wealth, and gain long-term financial stability.

passage.heading: 01 / The Affordability Problem
passage.text: Home prices and mortgage rates have pushed monthly payments beyond what many hardworking families can carry — even when their income, credit, and employment are strong. The usual "fix" is to loosen lending standards, which is exactly what fueled past housing collapses. The HOME Act rejects that trade-off: it lowers the monthly payment without lowering the standards that keep lending sound.

passage.heading: Capped Starter Rates
passage.text: When interest rates spike, first-time buyers are the first ones priced out — families with strong income and credit watch the same house drift out of reach. The HOME Act caps the interest rate on qualifying first-time homebuyer mortgages, backed by the same public-private financing as the HOME mortgage: Treasury-backed bonds and lender tax credits cover the difference, so lenders stay whole and standards stay sound.

passage.heading: Restore the American Dream.
passage.text: And for the families locked out the longest — first-time and working-family buyers — it opens three more doors: expanded FHA lending, a homebuyer tax credit, and a cap on starter rates.

passage.heading: 04 / The First-Time Buyer Package
passage.text: First-time buyers and working families face hurdles a lower payment alone can't fix: saving a down payment while paying rent, covering closing costs, and qualifying when rates spike. The HOME Act meets each one head-on. And every policy below follows the same rule as the HOME mortgage itself — more access, same sound lending standards.

passage.heading: Expanded FHA Lending
passage.text: FHA loans are how generations of American families bought a first home — low down payments, sound underwriting, and a public guarantee that makes lenders say yes. The HOME Act expands FHA lending for first-time buyers: loan limits that reflect what homes actually cost in communities like ours, lower mortgage-insurance premiums, and a simpler, faster approval process.

passage.heading: 05 / Frequently Asked Questions
passage.text: A lower monthly payment. Expanded FHA lending. A first-time homebuyer tax credit. Capped starter rates. The HOME Act proves families don't have to choose between affordable payments and responsible lending. Add your support and help restore the American Dream.
